Bundled model · trained from random weights on Track 1
What the neural network sees and learns

Eight road-relative observations: speed, wheel angle, lane offset, heading error, the road’s lateral and forward position at a speed-dependent lookahead, and two curvature measurements. The network predicts steering and a signed acceleration/braking command at 20 Hz. A 120 Hz physics loop applies those actions. Coordinates, track ID, and lap progress are excluded from the model’s inputs.

Training minimizes action prediction error against expert demonstrations. The evaluation compares each attempt with a clean reference lap using lane score, progress, off-track time, barrier contacts, lap time, action error, and lateral trajectory difference at matching track progress. Training uses a fixed dataset from Track 1; evaluation does not update weights.

This is a state-and-road-map model with perfect simulated road observations. It is not a camera-based vision model or a real-vehicle driving system. Recovery examples use expert-labelled perturbations; mirrored examples teach both turn directions. The bundled model was trained from random weights with Adam for 100 epochs.
